pr_body:
Fixes: https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/104995

This PR disables all the planning optimizations that rely on `Expression.nullable()`. 
The semantics of this QL API have changed significantly in ESQL, so for now we'll just remove all the code that uses it. See also comments [here](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/105023#issuecomment-1955640677)
pr_title: ES|QL: Disable optimizations that rely on Expression.nullable()
pr_comment: Hi @luigidellaquila, I've created a changelog YAML for you.

Thanks @astefan, makes sense.
I added unit tests for all the rules I changed, and I realized that I could simplify some overrides.

> The original method returns null IF the expression is nullable which is true for functions only if at least one child is null. However it is also true for attributes / FieldAttributes leading to its replacement with null.

@costin the problem is that we cannot rely on nullability logic. In ESQL an expression can be null also in other situations, eg. mv or number overflows.

> In might be that in the SQL planner this didn't get a chance kick in because of the other rules - one fix would be to change the nullify method.

The problem doesn't kick in in SQL for two reasons:
- in ESQL we have `PropagateEvalFoldables` that injects constants where SQL had attributes
- SQL can rely on nullability logic, ESQL cannot

I tried to change `nullify()`, but it didn't work: at that stage it's too late, I tried to summarize it in the [comments above](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/105691#discussion_r1515823851)
`elasticsearch-ci/rest-compatibility` finished and was green, but for some reason  GitHub after a few hours still didn't see it...
